label: 3-day, 100-year storm, change × model agreement
description: Change in rain in the 3-day, 100-year storm, counted in full where both climate models agree on the direction, halved where they disagree
details: NOAA Atlas 14 (model’s 1979–2005) → 2050–2079 · GFDL-CM3 and NCAR-CCSM4 · RCP 8.5 · × agreement on direction
method: Each model's percent change in the 3-day, 100-year storm from NOAA Atlas 14 to 2050–2079 (as Variant C, but kept per model: GFDL-CM3 and NCAR-CCSM4), then average change × agreement, where agreement = 1 if both models change in the same direction (both increase, or both decrease: an agreed decrease stays negative) and 0.5 if they disagree. The result stays in %: where the models agree on the direction it equals Variant C; where they disagree it is halved. Atlas 14 grid: annual maximum series.
pros: Counts the change in full where both models agree on the direction (up or down); halves it on the 18 % of land where they split
Draws on both models about equally (rank correlation about 0.7 with each), unlike the plain average, which follows GFDL-CM3
Same units as the plain change (%), so boundaries stay readable
cons: A modest correction: the same class as Variant C on 84–88 % of land, and 90–95 % of its High cells were High in C
Still two models only: agreement between two is a weak test
Where both models agree on an increase, the size of it is still their average, which leans on GFDL-CM3
sources: SNAP DOT precipitation frequency, local netCDFs (3d, 2050–2079, interval 100, both models)
author: Joshdpaul
